messages:
pagerduty: page fired -> oncall@region-az3 for alert: az3-serving-high-5xx-rate (auto-escalation: SEV2)
incident-bot: incident created (SEV2) · incident id: INC-20260315-az3-01 · runbook: az-fallback-guide.md
Jordan (SRE): ack. I'm on it, pulling logs now.
Marta P: Ack from secondary. E2E checks on regional router + LB health.
Alex R: seeing a spike in 502/504s from model-shard-proxy in az3-srv-*. CPU & net look normal, connections spiking.
Jordan (SRE): can you paste the nginx upstream errors/log tail?
Alex R: here —
```
[2026-03-15T14:22:08Z] proxy_502 upstream timed out for client 10.2.5.12
[2026-03-15T14:22:09Z] proxy_504 gateway timeout connecting to shard-12
[2026-03-15T14:22:11Z] upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response
```
Sam L: ok, quick triage: 1) route new requests away from az3 (failover/fallback) 2) check shard placement + redis k/v cache errors 3) notify CS for impacted customers. Who can flip the divert?
Alex R: running divert now to eu-west-2 as a soft failover (no config change to customers). Command: 
```
redwoodctl routing divert --from az3 --to eu-west-2 --duration 15m --policy soft-failover
```
Alex R: command issued, awaiting progress.
incident-bot: routing change initiated, job id rchg-87321. Health checks will re-evaluate every 15s.
Jordan (SRE): I'm tailing proxy logs to confirm connection drain. If divert holds, we'll keep at soft and evaluate promoting permanent routing shift.
Emma C (CS): heads-up: a handful of beta customers in AZ3 reported intermittent 502s ~14:20–14:25. I opened a support note and DM'd affected accounts. I'll update once we know customer impact.
Marta P: check cache (KV) evictions on the shards — I saw eviction spikes earlier this morning in az3 on shard-12.
Alex R: confirming eviction count jump around 14:18, likely causing backend retries. Logs: 
```
kvcache: eviction_threshold crossed: count=8123 -> evicting 512 entries
kvcache: shard-12 rehydrate started
```
Jordan (SRE): mitigation plan: 1) maintain routing divert 2) increase kvcache rehydrate concurrency on shard-12 3) throttle heavy batch workloads from az3 for 30m
Sam L: approve. Alex, please bump rehydrate concurrency and apply batch throttle policy. Add a short-lived canary route back after 10m.
Alex R: applied rehydrate delta: `kubectl patch deployment kvcache-shard-12 -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kvcache","env":[{"name":"REHYDRATE_CONCURRENCY","value":"8"}]}]}}}}'`
incident-bot: change rchg-87321 reports: divert active -> 64% of new traffic now away from az3. Health checks: failing instances: 7 -> re-evaluating.
Jordan (SRE): health improving on shard proxies, 5xx rate trending down from 12% to 3% in the last 2m. Keep monitoring.
Emma C (CS): posting status update to customers now: "We detected elevated error rates in one availability zone; traffic has been diverted and we're monitoring. No data loss reported." :white_check_mark:
Sam L: ok team — if metrics hold for next 10m we downgrade to mitigation monitoring and start post-incident analysis. Jordan, you own the postmortem. Marta, collect cache metrics, Alex capture the routing and kvcache commands we ran. Emma, bundle customer impact notes.
Jordan (SRE): acknowledged. I'll escalate to SEV2->SEV3 transition once stable and then assign incident doc.
incident-bot: incident INC-20260315-az3-01 marked: mitigation in progress. Next rotation: handoff to oncall@night (Sam L) at 18:00 UTC if still open.
Alex R: divert continues, 5xx now at 1.2%. Leaving soft-failover active, will prepare canary back to 10% in 12m.
Jordan (SRE): thanks. I'll keep a 1hr watch and then start the RCA draft.
Emma C (CS): tracking updated — sending proactive emails to impacted accounts with link to status page.
Sam L: thx all. please drop any lingering artifacts (logs, kvcache dumps) into the incident doc. :thumbsup:
Jordan (SRE): will do. closing slack loop here once we hit stable for 10m.
